messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into German, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE German line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Sie brachte mir so viel Schwere mit der Angst aus ihrem Anblick, dass ich die Hoffnung auf die Höhe verlor.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table (Italian → German)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|--------------------|------------------|--------| | **questa** | demonstrative pronoun, female agent “she” | Sie | “she” | OK | | **mi** | 1st sg. dative pronoun, experiencer “to me” | mir | “to me” | OK | | **porse** | remote past of *porre* “to give, cause” | brachte | “brought / caused” | OK | | **tanto** | adverb of quantity “so much” | so viel | “so much” | OK | | **di** (line 52) | preposition linking quantity to noun “of” (gravezza) | – (omitted) | – | **UNNECESSARY** (Italian preposition not needed in German) | | **gravezza** | noun “heaviness, weight” | Schwere | “heaviness” | OK | | **con** | preposition “with” introducing accompanying circumstance | mit | “with” | OK | | **la** | definite article, fem. sg. “the” (paura) | der | “the” (dative) | OK | | **paura** | noun “fear” | Angst | “fear” | OK | | **ch'uscia** | relative clause “that came out / emerged” | aus | “out of” (prepositional) | **UNNECESSARY** (verb of emergence omitted) | | **di** (line 53) | preposition “of / from” introducing source of fear | aus | “out of” | OK | | **sua** | possessive adjective “her” (vista) | ihrem | “her” | OK | | **vista** | noun “sight, view” | Anblick | “sight” | OK | | **ch'io** | relative conjunction + subject “that I” | dass ich | “that I” | OK | | **perdei** | remote past of *perdere* “to lose” | verlor | “lost” | OK | | **la** | definite article, fem. sg. “the” (speranza) | die | “the” | OK | | **speranza** | noun “hope” | Hoffnung | “hope” | OK | | **de** | preposition “of” linking hope to its object | auf | “on / of” | OK | | **l'altezza** | noun “the height” (metaphoric goal) | die Höhe | “the height” | OK |
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: - *di* (line 52) – the Italian preposition “di” is not expressed in the German clause “so viel Schwere”. - *ch'uscia* – the relative verb “uscia” (“came out”) is not rendered; the meaning is covered by the preposition “aus”, but the verb itself is omitted.
All other source tokens are correctly rendered in the German translation with appropriate grammatical agreement.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only German script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final German text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
